briefdescription.para: Fused implementation of the combining tree arrival and a reduction operation.

detaileddescription.para: The last thread arriving at a certain ticket (counter) moves on to the next level of the tree. When it does so, it reads the value written by the other thread that arrived at the same ticket, applies the reduction function, and writes the result to be used in the next level. When reaching the root, it stores the final value and returns true. Note that the left and right arguments to the reduction function are determined by the thread IDs, regardless of the order in which threads arrive. In other words, for a given number of threads, the order of the reduction operations is fully deterministic.

briefdescription.para: Generic implementation of arrive with custom completion function.

detaileddescription.para: The arrival function should return true when the thread is the last to arrive at the root of the tree. Returns a token that can be used to wait for the barrier to complete. The custom completion function is called by the last thread arriving at the root, before advancing the barrier phase and notifying all waiting threads.

detaileddescription.para: This is useful for debugging purposes to detect mismatched barrier calls, but should not really be used otherwise. If CYQLONE_SANITY_CHECKS_BARRIER is disabled, the line number is ignored and this function is equivalent to arrive(uint32_t). Each thread should use a unique thread ID in [0, expected-1].

briefdescription.para: Check if wait() may block.

detaileddescription.para:
If it returns false, the caller can call wait() and it will return immediately without spinning or sleeping. This is useful if the caller has other non-critical work to do while waiting for other threads. Users should still call wait() before arriving again.
This function does not impose any memory ordering, so even when it returns false, changes made before the arrival of other threads may not be visible yet. In contrast, wait() does ensure proper synchronization.

briefdescription.para: Wait for the barrier to complete after an arrival, using the given token.

detaileddescription.para: Separating the arrival and wait phases allows for overlapping computation with waiting, hiding the synchronization latency. Waiting on the same token multiple times is not allowed.

briefdescription.para: Fairly vanilla combining tree barrier.

detaileddescription.para:
It is inspired by GCC 15.2's __tree_barrier, with some important API differences:
Every thread has a unique thread ID in [0, expected-1]. This eliminates the need for hashing the pthread thread IDs and for the inner search loop to find free slots in the tree.
Wait tries to spin for a given number of iterations before falling back to a futex-based atomic wait.
The barrier phase is exposed to the user.
Custom completion functions can be provided at arrival time.
Reductions and broadcasts on small values are supported.
